sentences.text: Resource selection begins after the operational priority and essential response requirements have been confirmed.
The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents units whose reported status and capabilities match the incident requirements.
The Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays estimated travel times, unit availability, and relevant access constraints.
The Triage Supervisor confirms that the selected response level remains consistent with the caller information.
The selection decision weighs clinical need, travel time, vehicle capability, crew readiness, and regional coverage.
The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides current information about vehicles that are unavailable or restricted.
The Radio Coordinator checks that the proposed unit can be reached on the Regional Radio Network.
A dispatcher may recommend a unit, but dispatch authorization must follow the current regional approval rules.
The Shift Commander approves exceptions that would materially reduce local coverage or require a nonstandard response.
The Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical resource requirements when the incident presents an unusual care need.
The dispatcher records the authorized unit and any conditions attached to its assignment.
Regional Dispatch Center produces the Unit Staging Change Card when a previously selected unit must be repositioned.
The Radio Coordinator selects the appropriate talkgroup and confirms that it is available before transmitting.
The dispatch transmission states the incident identifier, location, priority, response assignment, and any immediate hazard information.
The Paramedic Crew acknowledges the assignment and repeats the location and priority for confirmation.
The dispatcher corrects any discrepancy through a fresh transmission rather than relying on an unclear acknowledgment.
If the assigned unit does not acknowledge promptly, the Radio Coordinator attempts contact again and alerts the dispatch supervisor.
The North Gate Status Board and South Gate Status Board support routing decisions when access conditions are changing.
Dispatchers state a confirmed gate or approach constraint explicitly and identify any uncertainty in the information.
The controlled handoff occurs when the crew has acknowledged the assignment and the dispatch floor has confirmed the essential details.
The Paramedic Crew reports any material conflict between the transmitted route and conditions observed in the field.
The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination information with the receiving Emergency Department when required.
Radio Coordinator sends the Coverage Gap Bulletin when available ambulance coverage falls below the regional threshold.
Juniper records the authorization time and the reason for selecting the assigned unit.
